`<Header />` reads a variable named `Header`. If nothing declares or imports it, usually because of a typo or a forgotten import, rendering throws a `ReferenceError`.

Names that start with a lowercase letter, such as `<div>` or `<my-element>`, are HTML elements and are not checked. In `<Menu.Item>`, only `Menu` is checked.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
export function Page() {
  return <Header title="Home" />;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import { Header } from "./header";

export function Page() {
  return <Header title="Home" />;
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowGlobals` | `false` | Accept components that are global variables. |

By default a global does not count in a module, even one you declared:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
/* global Header */

export function Page() {
  return <Header title="Home" />;
}
```

{/* good {"options": [{"allowGlobals": true}]} */}
```jsx
/* global Header */

export function Page() {
  return <Header title="Home" />;
}
```
